correctness.rationale: A face of Ind(C_n square K_q) is precisely a cyclic partial proper coloring with at most one nonzero color per vertex. Independently derived the weighted (q+1)-state transfer matrix whose nonzero color-sum-zero subspace has eigenvalue +1 with multiplicity f−1 and whose 2x2 empty/color-uniform block has trace 2−f and determinant 1; hence signed face sum Z_{n,f}=f−1+L_n(f), including f=0 via Z=1. The S_q action cannot permute distinct vertices within a simplex because each position appears at most once; simplices invariant under a permutation are fixed vertexwise and involve only f fixed colors. Burnside on face orbits yields tilde chi(Y)=−(1/q!)sum_f binom(q,f)D_{q−f}Z_{n,f}; empty fixed-point cases are handled via augmented Euler convention. For f<=4, both roots of t²−(2−f)t+1 have modulus one including double roots; power traces are bounded. For q>=5 the identity permutation f=q supplies the unique largest root rho_q=(q−2+sqrt(q(q−4)))/2>1, while nonidentity permutations have at most q−2 fixed colors, giving tilde chi~(−1)^(n+1)rho_q^n/q!. Alternating-sum inequality gives total reduced rational Betti >=|tilde chi|, without claiming exact homology. Independently enumerated canonical unlabeled partial proper circular words for all 42 (n,q) with n=3..8, q=1..7 and matched the Burnside formula; checked bounded Euler values q<=4 through n=199 and dominant root at q=5,6,7,n=80. The all-n proof uses matrix eigenvalues, not finite tests.

value.rationale: Global color relabeling produces a natural unlabeled partial-coloring simplicial orbit space, distinct from a naive combinatorial vertex quotient. Exact quotient Euler characteristics expose a sharp qualitative five-color transition and a concrete exponential lower bound on rational homology across an infinite graph family, a structural result rather than arbitrary finite tabulation.

limitations: n>=3,q>=1; proves Euler and exponential total rational Betti lower bound for q>=5, not individual Betti, torsion or exact homotopy type; small-q Euler boundedness says nothing about Betti boundedness.
